titulo: Could a Saltwater Crocodile Survive Every Prehistoric Era?

blocos.texto: The saltwater crocodile. Twenty feet long, one ton, the strongest bite of any living animal. Its family watched the dinosaurs rise and fall. So what happens if we drop it into every era of Earth's history? Would it rule? Or get eaten alive? Comment your guess for the worst era right now.

The rules. One hundred crocodiles per era. They need air they can breathe, warm water, and big prey. At the end of each era, a tier. S means they rule. F means they're gone. Pause and guess along with me.

The Cambrian. Five hundred million years ago. Land is bare rock. The top predator, Anomalocaris, is three feet long. A snack. But the real prey are trilobites the size of your thumb. A croc would need thousands a week. They starve. F tier.

The Ordovician. Now there's Cameroceras, a squid in a twenty foot shell, and giant sea scorpions. Food is better. But then the planet freezes. Cold blooded crocs in icy water just shut down. Another F.

The Devonian. The age of fish. Dunkleosteus, thirteen feet of armor with a bite that could cut sharks in half. In open water, our croc loses. But in rivers and lagoons, full of fish, it eats all day. B tier.

The Carboniferous. Thirty five percent oxygen. Millipedes eight feet long. Dragonflies with two foot wings. The whole planet is one giant warm swamp. For a crocodile? Paradise. What tier would you give? I say A.

The Permian. One supercontinent, a huge desert inside. The predator here has saber teeth, Inostrancevia. On land it's dangerous, in water the croc wins. But then the worst extinction ever hits. Ninety percent of sea life dies. C tier.
The Triassic. This is the crocodile's own family era. Croc relatives ruled before dinosaurs did. Warm rivers, ferns, lots of prey. Our crocs fit right in. A tier.
The Jurassic. Dinosaurs everywhere. On land, an Allosaurus wins. But every dinosaur needs to drink. And when it lowers its head to the river, the crocodile is waiting. A tier.

The Cretaceous. T. rex is here. But the real problem is in the rivers. Deinosuchus. A crocodile thirty five feet long that hunted dinosaurs. Next to it, our croc is a baby. Then the asteroid hits. And crocodiles survive it. B tier.
The Paleocene. A hot rainforest world. And Titanoboa, a snake forty two feet long. It could eat a young croc. But an adult bites back. Warm water, lots of fish. A tier.
The Miocene. In the ocean, Megalodon. Fifty feet. One bite. Saltwater crocs love to swim between islands. Here, that's suicide. Stay in the rivers, and you live. B tier.

The Ice Age. Sounds like the worst one, right? Wrong. The tropics stayed warm, and saltwater crocodiles actually lived here, next to Megalania, a lizard eighteen feet long. The lizard is extinct. The croc is still here. S tier.

Final list. S, the Ice Age. A, the swamps, the Triassic, the Jurassic and the Paleocene. B, the Devonian, the Cretaceous and the Miocene. C, the Permian. F, the Cambrian and the Ordovician. Did I get one wrong? Tell me in the comments, and tell me which animal goes through every era next.
